note: Parity baseline for the explorer theme and layout system, captured on the TOKENIZED tree (the token milestone landed) with the layout-aware probe revision: layout-derived keys (auto margins, declared cell widths) are recorded as layout-independent values, so hashes reproduce on a live chain regardless of content. Supersedes the pre-tokenization capture of the same date, which is preserved in git history. The same probe re-run after any CSS change must reproduce every hash below.
venue: an RDOGE regtest explorer, reached over an SSH tunnel at localhost:18080

layers.rule: every property DECLARED by an xchain.css / xchain-charts.css / themes rule, read back on the first element matching that rule's selector: as the computed value for most properties, and as the declared text resolved through the element's custom properties for state rules and for layout-derived properties (width/height/margins/offsets), whose getComputedStyle readback is the content-dependent USED value. Mode-independent by construction on the current tree.
layers.rend: a fixed anchor census (31 selectors x 23 properties) read as computed values regardless of which stylesheet won, except the layout-derived properties (margin-top/margin-bottom), which are read from the Typed OM computedStyleMap so an auto margin is recorded as "auto" rather than as its content-dependent slack. This layer does differ per mode, so it is the one that can see a dark/light regression.

coverage.why: 41 selectors are not instantiated by any captured page, re-measured on the tokenized tree (the pre-tokenization survey counted 121/77/44): the whole .xc-chart* family (no fragment creates a chart), the external-explorer glyphs, the #transaction detail table (its page rendered but the table never populated on this venue), the runtime-applied row colours (.bg-red/.bg-yellow), and a handful of one-off utility classes. Stated rather than hidden: the runtime layer cannot prove parity for a rule no page exercises, which is exactly why the static token-literal gate is a separate acceptance test and not a nicety.
